Release notes[¶](#release-notes "Link to this heading")

Pillow is released quarterly on January 2nd, April 1st, July 1st and October 15th. Patch releases are created if the latest release contains severe bugs, or if security fixes are put together before a scheduled release. See [Versioning](versioning.html#versioning) for more information.

Please use the latest version of Pillow. Functionality and security fixes should not be expected to be backported to earlier versions.

Note

Contributors please include release notes as needed or appropriate with your bug fixes, feature additions and tests.

To accomplish this task, we will use the `PIL` (Pillow) library. We will create an RGB image, use `ImageDraw` to draw the text, and use `textbbox` (the modern, recommended way to measure text size in Pillow) to get the dimensions. Finally, we will use the `resize` method with `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` for high-quality downsampling.

The following program performs these steps and prints the required information.

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

def main():
    # 1. Create an 800x600 RGB image in memory
    width, height = 800, 600
    image = Image.new("RGB", (width, height), color="white")
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)

    # 2. Draw the text 'Hello' with the default font
    text = "Hello"
    # Using default font
    font = ImageFont.load_default()
    
    # 3. Measure the pixel width and height of that text
    # textbbox returns (left, top, right, bottom)
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    text_width = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    text_height = bbox[3] - bbox[1]
    
    # Draw text at (0,0)
    draw.text((0, 0), text, fill="black", font=font)

    # 4. Resize the image to 200x150 with high-quality (Lanczos) downsampling
    resized_image = image.resize((200, 150), resample=Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)

    # Print the results
    print(f"Text size: {text_width}x{text_height} pixels")
    print(f"Final image size: {resized_image.size[0]}x{resized_image.size[1]} pixels")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
